claims.text: The labour-slack pre-read puts the unemployment rate exactly at its estimated natural rate, with a zero gap, so on a slack basis the market is neither tight nor loose — a neutral (hold) signal.
The unemployment gap is zero, confirming labour-market balance and arguing for a hold rather than a hike or cut.
Three- and twelve-month average payroll gains are running well below the stated breakeven pace, a cooling in hiring that leans dovish.
The Sahm indicator is very low, showing no recessionary labour-market deterioration — this limits the dovish case.
Initial claims remain low, consistent with a still-tight labour market, a modestly hawkish offset to the softer payrolls.
The unemployment rate is essentially flat versus a year ago, another balanced reading.
The committee's unemployment-rate projections sit flat at 4.1 across the horizon, near the longer-run 4.2, signalling an expected stable labour market consistent with a hold.
The latest statement characterises employment as resilient, with job gains matching the workforce and little change in unemployment — a neutral description supporting a hold on labour grounds.
claims.quote: Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.

output.summary: On the labour evidence the market looks balanced and argues mainly for a hold, with a slight dovish tilt. The slack pre-read shows unemployment at its natural rate (\"gap_pp: 0.0\"), the SEP projects the unemployment rate flat at 4.1 through 2029, and the September statement says \"Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little\" — all neutral. The one dovish signal is payrolls (50.7k three-month average) running well below the 75.0k breakeven pace, which cooling hiring tilts slightly dovish; it is partly offset by low initial claims (197.8k) and a near-zero Sahm reading (0.033) showing no deterioration. Net: a modest dovish lean of -2bp.

The only genuine dovish pull is payrolls (50.7k three-month average) running well below the 75.0k breakeven pace, partly offset by low claims (197.8k) and a near-zero Sahm reading signalling no deterioration. Hence a small dovish lean rather than a clear case for a cut.

July 29, 2026
Federal Reserve issues FOMC statement
For release at 2:00 p.m. EDT
Share
The Federal Open Market Committee approved the following statement for release by a 9 – 3 vote:
The Committee decided to maintain the target range for the federal funds rate at 3-1/2 to 3-3/4 percent, in support of the Federal Reserve's dual mandate. The Committee is continuing its policy of maintaining ample reserves in the banking system.
Economic activity is expanding at a solid pace despite elevated uncertainty that owes, in part, to the conflict in the Middle East. Productivity growth and capital investment are strong. Job gains have kept pace with the workforce, and the unemployment rate has changed little.
Inflation remains elevated relative to the Committee's 2 percent goal, in part reflecting supply shocks that have driven price increases in certain sectors, including energy. The Committee will deliver price stability.
Voting against the monetary policy action were Beth M. Hammack, Neel Kashkari, and Lorie K. Logan, who preferred to raise the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point at this meeting.
